Hi Mina,

Thanks — we have invoice INV-3087 on file (attached). Our payments team is preparing the wire but flagged a recurring issue on this corridor: intermediary/cover bank fees are being deducted en route which results in short payments to Redwood.

Questions:
- Do you want Globex to send as OUR (sender pays all fees) or SHA (shared) for this payment? Our local bank by default sends SHA on this corridor and won’t allow OUR on >$50k without manual approval.
- If SHA, do you prefer Redwood to gross-up (we add a one-time fee line) or to reconcile the short payment on next invoice?
- Which legal entity should we pay (Redwood Inference, Inc. — US or Redwood Inference Europe BV)? Also confirm EU VAT handling (we are EU-registered and can provide VAT ID if reverse-charge applies).

Also attaching a sample MT103 from a prior transfer showing a $32 intermediary deduction. I can attach our bank’s suggested wire template if that helps.

Best,
Diego Ramos

Hi Diego — thanks for the heads-up and the MT103 sample. Quick answers and a couple of asks below.

1) Entity: Please pay Redwood Inference Europe BV (our EU collections entity) — bank details below. We invoice Globex EU entity, so reverse-charge is likely. If you can share your VAT ID we’ll confirm VAT handling.

2) Fees: Our preference is to receive the full invoice amount (i.e., sender chooses OUR). We realize some corridors don’t allow OUR; when THAT happens we usually: (a) ask the payer to include an explicit remittance and MT103 showing intermediary; and (b) Redwood will either (i) gross-up next invoice only when the shortfall >€100, or (ii) accept small deductions and reconcile quarterly.

3) Currency: If you can pay in EUR to the IBAN below, that avoids FX and reduces correspondent markup. If paying USD to our USD account we’ll likely see additional correspondent conversion fees.

Hi Diego / Mina,

Finance here — quick alignment so Globex has clear instructions and we reduce back-and-forth:

- Preferred flow: Pay to Redwood Inference Europe BV in EUR (IBAN above). In that case, Redwood expects the full invoiced EUR amount. Please request YOUR if your bank supports it.

- If your bank defaults to SHA and intermediary deductions occur: expect deductions typically between €20–€50 for this corridor. Redwood policy is: we will absorb deductions up to €25 per transfer; any shortfall above that will be either (a) reconciled on the next invoice, or (b) billed as a separate recovery fee (we can agree).

- USD payments: if Globex must pay USD to Redwood Inc (US), please be aware correspondent banks can (a) deduct fixed correspondent fees (~$30–$60) and (b) apply FX conversion with markups. To avoid surprises pay in the invoice currency (EUR).

VAT: if Globex is VAT-registered in the EU and this is a B2B supply, use reverse-charge (we will supply our EU VAT ID once you share yours). Please attach your VAT ID in reply.

We can also accept a gross-up if Globex prefers to keep YOUR/SHA as-is — in that case please add the estimated intermediary fee as a separate line on the current payment and state it in the remittance. For recurring payments we can bake a 0.5% FX/reserve fee to cover these corridors — open to discussing for a standing instruction.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call today to finalize.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference

Diego — appreciate the detail and the MT103. Short answer and a pragmatic path forward: we don’t want to slow this payment. Proposed compromise:

1) For this invoice only: if your bank must send SHA, please proceed. Globex to include the MT103/remittance when you send payment. Redwood will accept the shortfall for this payment if deductions are <=$50. If the shortfall >$50, Finance (Laura) will raise an adjustment invoice for the delta.

2) For future invoices: let’s operationalize one of two long-term paths — either (A) Globex requests OUR for EUR payments where possible (we’ll tolerate manual approval lag for >€50k), or (B) Globex pays USD to Redwood Inc and we implement a standing 0.5% FX/reserve to cover expected correspondence fees and conversion spreads. Option B speeds clearance but introduces FX variability.

3) If you confirm you’ll provide your VAT ID we’ll confirm reverse-charge and not apply VAT. Please also send the actual MT103 once the transfer occurs so we can reconcile immediately.

If you’re available, we can lock this in on a 15-min call tomorrow — I’ll coordinate times.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
